1.w: A good name [is finer] than good ointment, and the day of [one’s] death than the day he was born.

2.w: Better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for this [is] the end of all men, and the one living will give [it] to his heart.

3.w: Better [is] sorrow than laughter, for by the sadness of the face, the heart is made good.

4.w: The heart of the wise [is] in a house of mourning, and the heart of fools [is] in a house of gladness.

5.w: Better to hear the rebuke of a wise one, than hearing a song of fools.

6.w: For like the sound of thorns under the pot, so [is] the laughter of the fool; and also this [is] vapor.

7.w: Surely oppression drives a wise one to madness, and a bribe destroys the heart.

8.w: Better the end of a thing than its beginning; better one long of spirit than one high of spirit.

9.w: Do not hurry in your spirit to become angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.

10.w: Do not say, “Why is it that the former days were better than these?” For [it is] not from wisdom [that] you ask about this.

11.w: Wisdom [is] good, with an inheritance, and profitable for those seeing the sun.

12.w: For in the shadow of wisdom [is as] in the shadow of silver, and the advantage of knowledge [is] that wisdom keeps alive her owners.

13.w: See the work of God, for who is able to make straight what He has made crooked?

14.w: In a day of prosperity, be in gladness, and in a day of evil, see also: This as well as this, God has made, for the reason that man cannot find out anything after him.

15.w: All I have seen in the days of my vapor: There is a righteous one perishing in his righteousness, and there is a wicked one living long in his wickedness.

16.w: Do not be overly righteous, and not overly wise yourself—why should you be desolate?

17.w: Do not be overly wicked, and do not be a fool—why should you die in [what is] not your time?

18.w: [It is] good that you should take hold of this, and also not loosen your hand from this; for the one who fears God will go forth from them all.

19.w: Wisdom gives more strength to the wise one than ten rulers who are in a city.

20.w: For [there is] not a righteous man on the earth who does good and does not sin.

21.w: Also, for all words that they might speak, do not give your heart, that you may not hear your servant belittling you.

22.w: For many times also your own heart has known that you also have belitted others.

23.w: All this I have tested by wisdom; I have said, “I shall be wise,” and it [was] far from me.

24.w: Far off [is] that which has been, and very deep—who can find it out?

25.w: I also turned my heart to know, and to search out, and to seek wisdom and reason, and to know the evil of foolishness and the folly of madness.

26.w: And I am finding more bitter than death the woman who, she [is] a snare and her heart [is] a net; her hands [are] bonds; The one who is good before the face of God escapes from her, and the one sinning will be captured by her.

27.w: Behold, this I have found, says Qoheleth, one to one to find out the reason—

28.w: that which my soul still has sought, and I have not found: One man from a thousand have I found, and a woman among all these I have not found.

29.w: See, this alone I have found: That God made man upright, and they have sought out many schemes.
